rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes sliding wear in a chloride solution at elevated temperature (e.g., 600°C), whereas the paper used reciprocating tribo-corrosion in deionized water at 25–100°C with a prior thermal-shock treatment. The intervention type (tribo-corrosion) is the same, but the specific lever (temperature regime, environment, and thermal history) is different.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies a chloride-containing solution at elevated temperature (e.g., 600°C) with pin-on-disc wear, while the paper used deionized water at 25, 50, and 100°C with reciprocating ball-on-flat sliding and a thermal-shock pre-treatment. The broad regime of tribo-corrosion at elevated temperature is shared, but the specific environment, temperature range, and loading mode differ substantially.
